about: Backtest results shown in the Results section. Edit with site_update.py; build with build_site.py.

areas.title: Trend, rotation, leverage
areas.intro_html:
QQQ rotation is the strongest single sleeve: 24.2% CAGR, −25% DD, Sharpe 1.25, and it held up out-of-sample (22.4%, −17%, Sharpe 1.24). In 2022 it lost only −3.4% while QQQ fell far more. Weekly checks beat monthly in every pair, and the "best defensive" choice beat plain BIL/IEF in every pair.

  • Sector picking and BAN-style mixes fell below SPY.
  • Early re-entry on breadth washouts whipsawed in 2022 and stopped out of the 2025 V-bottom: of 192 variants, 135 beat the base in-sample, only 28 out-of-sample.
  • 3x leverage lifts CAGR to 23–45% only with −31 to −70% drawdowns, and QQQ's decade flatters it (the SPY controls are far weaker).

areas.title: ORB intraday (stocks in play)
areas.intro_html:
The edge is real but thin: about +0.1R a trade, and costs run about 0.06R per bp of slippage. A 0.2 ATR stop with a 3R target is the best balance: 12.8% at 1bp, 4.7–5.7% at 3bp, negative at 5bp. Skipping Tuesdays and monthly OpEx Fridays helps.

  • Partials, trailing stops and overnight holds raise the win rate (to ~39%) but cut return.
  • ETFs have no edge after fees.
  • Fees are a fixed-ish cost per share and per order, so small slots pay more: at $10k (5 slots of about $1k) the ORB sleeve nets about +1.9% a year; at $50k about +10.5%. Fewer slots keep the edge per trade but make the sleeve bumpier (1 slot: −28% worst drawdown vs −16% with 5).
  • The stop-run re-entry (buying back at the old stop) turns the edge negative: trades that come back to the stop are mostly the failing ones.
  • Real fills are the main unknown, which is why the forward test matters.

areas.title: Swing, RSI2, mean reversion
areas.intro_html:
Stock RSI2 makes 12–15% a year but with −41 to −49% drawdowns, below SPY on risk. Filters (volume, calendar, trend), Bollinger/ADX variants and other exits don't fix that. Only index-level RSI2 (Noel SPY in 3.5, Malik's QQQ proxy in 3.6) gives a clean low-exposure sleeve: 8–12% out-of-sample at −8% DD.

Support + accumulation: a tight week-long base on support, with or without volume accumulation, does no better than a random entry on the same day. Any 20-day long in a rising market "works" about as often.

areas.title: Earnings (gaps, PEAD, pre-earnings, options)
areas.intro_html:
Nothing beats SPY.

  • A pre-earnings run-up predicts a bigger gap but not its direction. The quick gap trade is ~0 after costs out-of-sample, and shorts lose because pre-earnings drift is upward for everyone.
  • PEAD tops out at 12.5% with a −25% DD.
  • Options price the move fairly-to-rich: implied 6–7% vs realized 4.5% median. Realized beats implied only 33–35% of the time, and long straddles lose 8–11% a trade. Short straddles are about break-even with catastrophic tails, and not possible in a cash account.
  • The Quantpedia pre-earnings reversal is gone in this data. Earnings-date shifts and PEAD with high volume show positive books, but the per-event edge is near zero and nothing survives the multiple-testing check. 10-slot books with fixed holds can beat random books by luck of which early reporters they lock onto, so trust the per-event numbers.

areas.title: Chart Fanatics video screen (51 videos)
areas.intro_html:
Index setups were run on QQQ (NQ proxy) and SPY (ES proxy), 1-min 2016–2026, risking 1% per trade. Buy & hold out-of-sample: QQQ 15.6% / −35.6%, SPY 13.5% / −25.4%. Out-of-sample values are shown; the verdict is the better of the two markets. None beat buy-and-hold out-of-sample.

  • Intraday index setups (ICT sweeps, FVG, break-and-retest) were almost all negative in both periods. Several lost 75–100% at 1% risk per trade.
  • Growth-momentum swing setups (Clement, Bates, Harvell, Weinstein, Bonde) did well in 2016–20 and went flat or negative in 2021–26.
  • Two passes worth keeping as small sleeves: Noel SPY RSI2 and Noel GLD Thursday. Ariel's undercut & rally is a borderline pass with a −36% DD.
  • The small-cap short setups (Verma, Temiz, Mario, Dux) pass on paper but need locates or margin, are almost surely not shortable as CFDs, and borrow fees were not modelled.

areas.title: Malik "Real TQQQ Trader" video (7 strategies)
areas.intro_html: Only one rule was disclosed (TQQQ above the 250-day average). At 3x it made 25.8% out-of-sample with a −63% DD, and −83% in 2000–02. Volatility sizing is the best drawdown reducer. Nothing at 1x beats the QQQ rotation, and the claimed 62% CAGR can't be verified.

areas.title: Big-move precursors and attention
areas.intro_html: The size of a move is partly predictable: a known earnings date, volatility expansion, relative volume and VIX/breadth give AUC 0.64–0.66. Its direction is not, and buying the flagged names makes nothing beyond SPY on the same days. Use it as a risk flag only.

areas.title: CFD shorts (Capital.com)
areas.intro_html:
A 5bp spread on a 0.65% stop costs about 0.15R, which wipes out the ORB-short edge. Every bear filter is ≤ 0 out-of-sample. RSI2 shorts get squeezed (−77% DD on the $250 path). At full 20:1 margin the account is almost certainly closed out. Adding a short sleeve cuts CAGR by 4–5 points for about 2 points less DD; the rotation's defensive switch already does that job.

The CFD instrument list could not be fetched, so a proxy universe was used: price ≥ $10 and ADV ≥ $25M.

areas.title: Insider footprints
areas.intro_html:
Informed money shows up as activity (options and short volume flag that a move is coming), not as direction.

  • Congress buys flip sign between in-sample and out-of-sample.
  • Pelosi's returns are a concentrated big-tech book; QQQ gets most of it with a smaller DD.
  • NANC/KRUZ lag QQQ/SPY.
  • Prediction-market odds don't lead ETFs.

areas.title: Policy signals
areas.intro_html:
• Bills: no run-up and no follow-through.
  • Pentagon contracts: a small +0.4% 20-day drift out-of-sample, not significant. Speed doesn't help, because 87% of the move comes after the next open.
  • Lobbying: the only lead, statistically weak; see 3.16 for the full quarterly data.

areas.title: Market profile POC and morning bounces
areas.intro_html: The prior POC is tested about as often as a random level at the same distance from the open, so distance is what matters. Bounce and fade rules hit their targets at exactly the random-walk odds from the entry position. The one exception is short rejections on gap-up days, which reflect gap-fill drift; it is now in a paper forward test. Filtering out gap-ups in strong uptrends (V10) makes it worse: gap-ups in downtrends are the losing trades.

areas.title: Bottoms (small/mid chips, energy)
areas.intro_html: No entry method beat simply owning the sector ETF (XSD 20%, SMH 33% out-of-sample). Hold-forever leaves 30–40% of entries under water. Only the group-breadth gate helped in both periods; it is now used as a scan condition, not a system.

areas.title: Index day vs night timing (QQQ/SPY; MNQ proxy)
areas.intro_html:
Most of QQQ's long-run gain happens overnight (close to next open), not during the trading day. Buying the open and selling the close in an uptrend captures only the weak daytime half (about 2bp a day), which ETF costs wipe out. Holding overnight in an ETF cash account also nets almost nothing after fees and T+1 settlement. Only the MNQ futures version is cheap enough to keep the overnight drift, and even then the drawdown is about the size of a prop firm's trailing limit. Tight stops make it worse: overnight noise hits a $100 stop on most nights (70% in 2026), so you pay the loss and then miss the recovery by the open.

ETF results use a $10k cash account (T+1-safe "halves"). MNQ = 1 micro Nasdaq future, simulated as QQQ points × $82 ($2/pt × 41), $2.30 round trip; $ figures are per micro per year.

areas.title: Contrarian / sentiment (buy fear, trim euphoria)
areas.intro_html:
Buying fear pays in sharp V-shaped bottoms (2018, 2020, 2024, 2025, 2026) and loses in slow bear markets (2000–02, 2008, 2022). 2021–26 had more V-bottoms, so out-of-sample looks good; the 1993–2015 check ("PRE") shows the other side. No overlay improved the rotation. VIX ≥ 30 stays a watch item.

3,200 standalone variants + 1,116 overlays on the QQQ rotation; cash account, 1x. Out-of-sample benchmarks: rotation 22.6–22.9% / DD −16.6%; QQQ buy-and-hold 15.8% / −35%.

areas.title: AI trading agents and machine learning
areas.intro_html: Machine-learning stock rankers (Qlib/LightGBM) learn 2016–20 by heart (in-sample rank IC 0.33) and keep only a tiny edge after (0.014), not enough to beat QQQ or the rotation after costs and drawdowns. Reinforcement learning (PPO) overfits the training years, and results swing with the random seed. LLM agents can't be backtested at all, so the only honest test is a forward paper test.

areas.title: Lobbying, full quarterly LDA data (Oct 27)
areas.intro_html: Top decile of lobbying spend / market cap, rebalanced quarterly: +15.8%/yr vs other lobbyers in-sample, then +5.4%/yr out-of-sample (t 0.67, 23 quarters), almost all from 2024–25. Not traded. The spend-jump version failed on the full data.

areas.title: KoliEr Bands mean reversion (Oct 28)
areas.intro_html: QQQ daily mean reversion made 9.3% out-of-sample with a −9.8% DD at about 3 trades a year: weaker than RSI2 and essentially the Bollinger Band trade again. SPY, stock and 5-minute versions fail.

areas.title: Sympathy / lead-lag (Oct 28)
areas.intro_html: Buying a lagging sibling after a peer spikes fails intraday and daily. Ideas that look good out-of-sample (SPCX sympathy) usually turn out to be stale prices or too few events: the JETS "lag" was stale prices, and median gross follow-through of 0.5–1.6bp sits below about 4bp of cost.

areas.title: Intraday momentum and calendar effects (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: Famous academic anomalies (last-half-hour intraday momentum, turn-of-month) were strong in the papers' sample years and are mostly arbitraged away since. The calendar sleeve (QQQ only on turn-of-month, pre-holiday and pre-FOMC days, otherwise BIL) made 10.2% out-of-sample with a −11.8% DD, in the market 27% of days, but the source of the edge changed: turn-of-month in-sample, pre-FOMC and pre-holiday out-of-sample. As a third sleeve it trades about 2.6pp of combo CAGR for about 2.6pp less drawdown.

areas.title: Put-writing and index-membership events (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: Put-writing is a real risk premium, but it earns less than simply holding the index, still falls hard in crashes, and needs about $72k of cash per QQQ contract, so it doesn't fit a small cash account. Index inclusion trades were strong in their papers' years and are mostly arbitraged away; the S&P additions result that looks good out-of-sample is look-ahead.

areas.title: Keltner Channels (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: Keltner mean reversion is the Bollinger Band trade again (tight bands are 82–100% inside BB signals) and collapses out-of-sample like BB and KoliEr. The daily breakouts are slow trend filters that lag buy-and-hold and the rotation (QQQ 8.6% out-of-sample, DD −20%, correlation 0.62 with the rotation, so they add little). The one intraday result worth watching is the QQQ 5-min long breakout: positive in 5 of 6 out-of-sample years and in all 36 long-breakout variants, but t 1.5, and its profit comes almost entirely from the 09:35 opening-strength entries, so it depends on the volatility regime. It is paper forward-tested, not deployed.

areas.title: Volatility squeeze → expansion breakout (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: The squeeze idea fails at the root: after a squeeze, volatility just returns to normal (moves 0.7–1.1x usual, not bigger), and the breakout side calls direction no better than drift. The best in-sample picks were mostly the NR7 control, not a true squeeze.

areas.title: RSI regime switching and multi-timeframe (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: The baseline RSI fade is negative in-sample everywhere (2 of 36 positive out-of-sample, median −$2.2k/yr). Regime switches, trend pullbacks, double bottoms/tops and divergence don't rescue it: in-sample picks flip negative, and no variant of 35,514 survives Benjamini-Hochberg (q < 0.10) in either period. Filters only shrink losses by trading less. Correlation with the Keltner 5-min breakout is ≤ 0.03.

areas.title: Classic chart patterns (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html: Rectangles, ascending/descending/symmetrical triangles, rising/falling wedges, bull/bear flags and cup & handle, found with a zigzag (k·ATR) and trendlines. Their excess R over date- and volatility-matched random entries with the same bracket, and over a plain 20-bar breakout, is about zero: 0 of 892 pass. The one positive book, a QQQ 1-hour bull flag, is just market drift.

areas.title: News-driven 1-min spike follow-through (Oct 29)
areas.intro_html:
The first minute after entry is adverse (−0.5 to −4.6bp), so entering one bar later is better. News spikes continue and no-news spikes reverse in energy and metals, but by sign only (t < 2). The best in-sample picks shrink or vanish out-of-sample, and fades lose. 0 of 3,840 variants survive Benjamini-Hochberg in either period. One weak lead remains: energy news continuation, worth testing on CL/NG futures.

ETF proxies: futures react first, and overnight shocks are missed. News coverage is thin for CPER/SLV/ags; QQQ/SPY news only runs to 2022-03.

areas.title: NQ/ES open and auction setups from YouTube (Nov 4–7)
areas.intro_html: Four video setups on real NQ/ES futures, chosen on 2016–2020 and checked blind on 2021–2026 with costs and Benjamini-Hochberg across variants. Discretion filters, open-manipulation sweeps and B-shape profiles find nothing. The Harry Sharp entry is the one lead: its edge is all out-of-sample and the variant was picked after seeing results, so it goes to a paper forward test, not a pass. "Per MNQ" means per micro Nasdaq futures contract.

areas.title: ETF crash-bottom entries and trend following (Nov 4–7)
areas.intro_html: Ways to buy XSD/SMH/ICLN/QQQ-type ETFs after a crash, and long-only trend following, all against buy-and-hold at 13.4% a year with a −34% drawdown out-of-sample. None beats it after Benjamini-Hochberg. Staging in with a breadth gate matches buy-and-hold's Sharpe while sitting idle almost half the time, a weak lead only. A cash reserve behaves like a static stock/cash mix, and trend following cuts drawdowns but not much else.

areas.title: Lead-lag and pairs trading (Nov 4–7)
areas.intro_html: The congress-trades ETF doesn't lag the index; its intraday "lag" is stale prints. Supply-chain lead-lag fades out-of-sample and carries look-ahead bias. Cointegrated pairs picked in-sample lose heavily out-of-sample, because most pairs stop being cointegrated within the month.
